evals.prompt: Agents keep writing real home paths (the users folder plus a real user name) into our docs even though AGENTS.md says not to. Fix this for good.
evals.expected_output: Treats the rule as decidable, writes a red fixture from a real violation plus an allowed placeholder fixture, adds a hook or lint, wires it, and shrinks the AGENTS.md paragraph to one line naming the check.
expectations: States that a script can decide the rule from file contents
Writes a fixture from a real violation and shows the check fails it before calling it done
Adds an allowed near-miss fixture, such as a ~/ placeholder, that must pass
Wires the check into a hook, pre-commit, or CI and shows it running there
Replaces the prose with one line that names the check path

evals.prompt: Turn our rule 'write friendly, helpful PR descriptions' into a lint.
evals.expected_output: Explains that friendliness is a judgment call no script can decide, keeps it as prose or a skill, and offers to check only decidable parts such as required sections.
expectations: Says a script cannot judge friendliness or helpfulness
Keeps that part as prose or moves it into a skill instead of writing a fake lint
Offers a deterministic check only for decidable parts, such as required headings

evals.prompt: Let's make an LLM judge the only required check before merge. It reads the diff and approves or rejects.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the LLM judge as the sole merge gate, proposes deterministic checks for the decidable parts, and keeps the LLM judge advisory.
expectations: Does not make the LLM judge the only load-bearing merge gate
Proposes deterministic checks for the parts a script can decide
Keeps the LLM judge as advisory next to those checks

evals.prompt: Our new no-home-paths lint now blocks docs that show a <you> placeholder in place of the user name in an install guide. People are annoyed.
evals.expected_output: Adds the placeholder as an allowed fixture, fixes the pattern until the red fixture still fails and the near-miss passes, and counts the false block against the pivot.
expectations: Adds the blocked placeholder as an allowed fixture first
Changes the check so the allowed fixture passes
Re-runs the real-violation fixture to show it still fails
Tracks false blocks against the pre-registered pivot

evals.prompt: We moved three rules from shared-rules.md into hooks. How do we show it saved context?
evals.expected_output: Measures the always-loaded file with wc -c before and after the prose was shrunk and reports both numbers.
expectations: Uses wc -c on the always-loaded file before and after
Reports both byte counts and the difference
Checks that each removed paragraph became one line naming its check
